The `indexOf('.')` method returns the index of the first '.' in `property`, or -1 if none exists. After adding 1, the resulting `beginIndex` is either 0 (if no '.' is present) or a value between 1 and the length of `property` inclusive (if a '.' is present, because the dot's index is at most `length-1`). Java's `substring(int beginIndex)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` only when `beginIndex` is negative or greater than the string length. In this context, `beginIndex` is always non-negative and never exceeds the length: if no dot, beginIndex=0 ≤ length; if dot at the last character, beginIndex=length, which is allowed. Therefore, the exception condition is fully avoided.
